Proposed API
GET reference

In-App Purchase Offer Codes

Read in-app purchase offer code custom code information

Read in app purchase offer code custom code information as a flat JSON object.

GET/purchase-custom-codes/{purchaseCustomCodeId}

Proposed · Extended read design · Adapter not implemented

Request

Routes are relative to your connection. Use a facade API key; the service manages Apple authentication.

cURL
BASE='https://asc.example.com/v1/connections/conn_example'

curl --fail-with-body "$BASE/purchase-custom-codes/purchase_custom_code_123" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ASC_FACADE_KEY"
JavaScript
const base = "https://asc.example.com/v1/connections/conn_example";
const response = await fetch(`${base}/purchase-custom-codes/purchase_custom_code_123`, {
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ASC_FACADE_KEY}` }
});

const body = await response.json();
if (!response.ok) {
  throw new Error(body.error?.message ?? `HTTP ${response.status}`);
}
console.log(body);
Python
import json
import os
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from urllib.error import HTTPError

base = "https://asc.example.com/v1/connections/conn_example"
request = Request(
    f"{base}/purchase-custom-codes/purchase_custom_code_123",
    headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.environ['ASC_FACADE_KEY']}"},
)
try:
    with urlopen(request) as response:
        print(json.load(response))
except HTTPError as error:
    detail = json.load(error)
    raise RuntimeError(detail["error"]["message"]) from error

asc.example.com is a placeholder for your deployment. Examples use fictional IDs.

Path parameters

NameTypeDescription
purchaseCustomCodeIdRequiredstringThe selected resource’s ID.

Query parameters

NameTypeDescription
fieldsOptionalstringComma-separated attribute names to return. This selects read fields and does not expand relationships. Multiple values are comma-separated.
ValuescustomCode, numberOfCodes, createdDate, expirationDate, active

Response

One flat object for the selected resource.

200 · application/json
{
  "id": "in_app_purchase_offer_code_custom_code_123",
  "customCode": "custom_code_example",
  "numberOfCodes": 1,
  "createdDate": "2026-10-14T12:00:00Z",
  "expirationDate": "2026-10-14",
  "active": false
}

Illustrative response. Optional read fields may be absent or null; unknown enum values are preserved.

Response fields

NameTypeDescription
idstringApple’s resource ID. Keep this string unchanged when addressing a resource.
customCodestringThe custom code value reported by Apple for this resource.
numberOfCodesintegerThe number of codes value reported by Apple for this resource.
createdDatestring · date-timeWhen Apple created this resource, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
expirationDatestring · dateWhen this build expires for testing, as an RFC 3339 timestamp.
activebooleanWhether Apple marks this resource as active.
createdByActorIdOptional linkagestring | nullID of the related created by actor. Present only when Apple supplies linkage; related objects are not loaded automatically.
deactivatedByActorIdOptional linkagestring | nullID of the related deactivated by actor. Present only when Apple supplies linkage; related objects are not loaded automatically.

Behavior

  • A nested resource must belong to the selected parent and the configured connection. The adapter validates ownership before returning data.

Upstream route and translation

The adapter calls GET /v1/inAppPurchaseOfferCodeCustomCodes/{id}. Read Apple’s original endpoint ↗

Flatten Apple’s attributes into each resource object. Expose supplied singleton linkage as IDs, with no automatic relationship traversal. Read access does not make these fields writable.
